entry.content:

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - August 20, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 CNA Singapore and India discuss bilateral cooperation on semiconductors, food security at ministerial meeting The two countries signed Memorandums of Understanding on food safety and maritime heritage at the fourth India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable held in Singapore. Semiconductor Read
2 TechAsia The real risk for AI companies is running out of cash Stratechery founder Ben Thompson explains why AI companies could run out of cash before demand fades, and how pricing and supply chains factor in. AILogistics Read
3 TechAsia Meta launches AI tools for small businesses Meta said the features are free to use now. AI Read
4 TechAsia SoftBank, Ericsson validate AI software on 5G The companies said the AI-native scheduler adjusts downlink transmission settings in real time inside the radio access network, or RAN. AI Read
5 DigiTimes AMEC profit jumps 300%: China chip equipment maker expands beyond etch with US$520M plan Advanced Micro-Fabrication Equipment Inc. China (AMEC) posted a 300% surge in first-half 2026 profit and announced a CNY3.5 billion (US$520 million) capacity expansion, accelerating its shift from an etch specialist into a broader semiconductor equipment supplier. Semiconductor Read
6 CNA Why the suit is making a comeback – and becoming easier to wear Women’s tailoring is loosening up, with softer cuts, oversized silhouettes and lighter fabrics making the suit more versatile than ever. Semiconductor Read
7 DigiTimes AI drives network equipment demand as parts shortages deepen AI data center expansion and rising demand for enterprise network upgrades continue to lift the network equipment market, giving several vendors better order visibility. But surging prices for key components such as memory and PCBs, along with hyperscalers drawing heavily on supply-chain resources, are squeezing parts ElectronicsAI Read
8 DigiTimes SK Hynix's new HBM team lands in Nvidia and AMD's backyard — co-design is becoming the way to win HBM4 orders SK Hynix is reported to be assembling a high-bandwidth memory (HBM) design team in Silicon Valley, a move that would deepen its co-design work with major US chip customers. Analysts see it as evidence that HBM competition is shifting into a customized, jointly developed phase. Semiconductor Read
9 CNA Robots poised for 'ChatGPT moment', says Unitree CEO The industry is nearing a breakthrough where robots can be placed in unfamiliar environments and complete most tasks through simple voice or text instructions, says Unitree CEO Wang Xingxing. Automation Read
10 EETAsia Protecting Semiconductor Yield Through High-Purity Fastener Selection High-purity fastener materials and vented designs can help semiconductor manufacturers manage corrosion, thermal stress, contamination and vacuum-related risks across demanding fabrication environments The post Protecting Semiconductor Yield Through High-Purity Fastener Selection appeared first on EE Times Asia . Semiconductor Read
11 EETAsia NFC Market Set to Reach $37.4B by 2032 NFC adoption is accelerating across payments, consumer electronics and connected devices, driving sustained global market growth through 2032. The post NFC Market Set to Reach $37.4B by 2032 appeared first on EE Times Asia . Electronics Read
12 EETAsia AI Workloads Reshaping the Memory Hierarchy AI workloads are driving memory diversification, with HBM, LPDDR, DDR, and storage balancing capacity, latency, power, and cost. The post AI Workloads Reshaping the Memory Hierarchy appeared first on EE Times Asia . AI Read

Biotechnology Read

AIAutomation Read

This is a significant reduction from earlier plans by Nvidia to guarantee US$250 billion for the project, alth AI Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - August 15, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 CNA India PM Modi woos youth with free coaching, AI training Speaking weeks after massive youth-led protests forced the education minister to resign, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the initiative was aimed at easing the financial burden on millions of families. AI Read
2 TechAsia Goldman Sachs in talks on Nvidia’s $500b AI plan Nvidia has said it has the option to backstop up to US$125 billion, or 25% of potential deals. AI Read
3 TechAsia Nvidia scales back data center guarantee plans: report Separately, OpenAI’s Stargate project with Oracle and SoftBank Group is a US$500 billion US AI infrastructure effort expected to exceed 9 gigawatts by 2029. AI Read
4 DigiTimes Research insight: Delta, Lite-on raise capex to 9% of revenue in AI data center power race The speed of AI data center deployment is raising the bar for power and cooling suppliers. Chipmakers such as Nvidia and AMD are refreshing platforms annually, with each generation bringing sharp increases in power density and thermal requirements. Suppliers that cannot match that pace in R&D or capacity deployment ris AISemiconductor Read
5 DigiTimes Memory supply crunch pushes long-term contracts beyond the big three The global memory supply shortage is intensifying, with long-term agreements (LTAs) rapidly expanding beyond the three major memory manufacturers—Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Micron Technology—to include Sandisk, Nanya Technology Corporation, and China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT). Electronics Read
6 DigiTimes AI server tracker: Demand drives July revenue gains across Taiwan infrastructure suppliers Data center infrastructure providers reported revenue gains across baseboard management controllers (BMCs), optical modules, power supply components, and thermal management products. Some companies, such as LandMark Optoelectronics and Auras Technology, reported year-over-year July revenue growth exceeding 100%. Electronics Read
